input.model_so_far: Main shaft complete with the dog-clutch sleeve and gear-red-P between gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M.

new_parts.name: axle-input-T
new_parts.position: a short shaft below and parallel to the main shaft, through bracket-G's round hole, sticking out the bottom of the frame

new_parts.name: gear-blue-U
new_parts.catalog_name: Technic Gear 20 Tooth Double Bevel with Clutch on Both Sides
new_parts.position: on axle-input-T, meshing upward with gear-gray-L

what_each_new_part_touches: axle-input-T turns in bracket-G's round hole~
gear-blue-U's round hole goes onto axle-input-T~
gear-blue-U's teeth mesh with gear-gray-L's teeth
where_everything_is_after: axle-input-T, gear-blue-U: new, a second shaft below the main one, meshing into it

why.problem_solved: Adds the input: a hand- or motor-turned shaft that drives the main gear shaft through gear-gray-L.
why.why_these_parts: A double-bevel gear meshes cleanly with gear-gray-L's plain teeth at this close spacing; its own clutch faces aren't used here, just its teeth.
why.sets_up_for_later: axle-input-T's free end takes an output-style extension in step 11, making it an external handle. This is the gearbox's drive input.

review_note: Read as meshing with gear-gray-L specifically (not gear-red-P) because gear-blue-U sits lower and further left in the picture, closer to gear-gray-L's position near the frame. Whether gear-blue-U actually reaches gear-red-P's teeth too (both are 16-tooth, so a wide double-bevel gear spanning the gap between them is plausible) is not confirmed -- if it does, the clutch selects between two gears that are both already being turned by the same input, which would change the design from 'speed select' to 'engage/disengage'. This is the open mechanism question in systems.json.
